question: The marked price of an article is 35% above its cost price. After giving a 20% discount on the marked price, it is sold for Rs. 432. What is the cost price of the article?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

Let, the cost price = 100 units

∴ Market price = 100 + 100 of 35% = 135 units

The selling price = 135 - 135 of 20% = 108 units

So, 108 units = Rs. 432

⇒ 100 units = (432/108) × 100 = Rs. 400

∴ The cost price of the article is Rs. 400

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

The marked price of an article is 35% above its cost price

The selling price = Rs. 432

**Formula used:**

S.P. = (100 - Discount%)/100 × M.P.

**Calculation:**

Let, the cost price of the article = x

Then, the market price = 135x/100

So, (135x/100) × [(100 - 20)/100] = 432

⇒ (135x/100) × (80/100) = 432

⇒ x = 432 × (100/135) × (100/80)

⇒ x = 400

**∴ The cost price of the article is Rs. 400**
